violation_type.title: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised (26 TAC §746.1003(4))
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it was determined the director is in charge of a group of children in a classroom on a daily basis. Being in a classroom at all times prevents the director from   conducting their responsibilities which includes supervising staff.

finding_variants.text: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it was determined the director is in charge of a group of children in a classroom on a daily basis. Being in a classroom at all times prevents the director from   conducting their responsibilities which includes supervising staff.

This standard was reviewed during a DFPS and found deficient.  The director is not ensuring that all employees are being properly supervised. Employees have been allowed to be present without background checks on several occasions and have been informed by persons in charge to leave if state arrives.
There was sufficient evidence found during the DFPS investigation to show that an employee was not supervised by the director.
During an investigation it was determined that the director did not meet responsiblilities when a parent informed her of concerns they had involving an incident with their child and an employee.
Based on information gathered during the DFPS investigation, the director is not ensuring all employees are supervised during hours of operation to ensure children are safe.

The director was not properly supervising employees to ensure they were fulfilling their duties and responsibilities. The director did not report to parents about an incident involving inappropriate discipline in a classroom.

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: The director did not ensure that caregivers were conducting routine checks of children in care, resulting in a child being left unsupervised.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: During the course of the investigation, none of the staff members, including caregivers, the person in charge, and Center Directors, could identify who the caregiver was working with in the classroom.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, the minimum standard was determined to be deficient. The operation had implemented procedures requiring caregivers to contact administrative staff prior to taking children outside during periods of extreme heat or when a heat advisory was in effect. However, despite these procedures being in place, a caregiver was able to take a classroom of children outside without obtaining approval from administrative staff. As a result, a child was left unsupervised on the playground for approximately 14 minutes after the remainder of the classroom returned indoors. This incident demonstrated that the operation?s implemented procedures were not effectively monitored or followed to ensure children were protected from potential risks associated with outdoor play during extreme weather conditions and that all children remained accounted for during transitions.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on evidence obtained a caregiver did not discipline children at naptime appropriately, the director stated that she was aware that naptime was the hardest time for the caregiver, yet did not supervise the employee appropriately, thus leading to the inappropriate use of discipline to children during naptime.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: This standard was evaluated as part of the investigation and this standard was found to be deficient when a caregiver left a child on the playground.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on evidence gathered from the DFPS investigation, a lack of director supervision resulted in a caregiver allowing inappropriate behavior between children to occur.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation. The director did not provide the appropriate supervision of staff that caused caregivers to perform responsibilities inappropriately.

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: It was found through investigation that a concern was raised about an employee and the director did not ensure the concerns were addressed in a way that resolved the issue.

Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, the director failed to ensure all employees were supervised. The director was unaware an incident where a caregiver placed an infant in a baby jumper that tipped over with the infant inside. The director was also not aware of incidents were the a caregiver left infants unattended on a diaper changing table, placed prohibited items (boppy pillows, bottles, and blankets) in cribs with infants, used profane and inappropriate language in the presence of children . According to the director, they were not aware of anything going on with the caregiver until CCR informed them of the allegations.

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: A person identified as a volunteer caregiver was counted in child/caregiver ratio while not having current CPR/First Aid training. This person was also found asleep while caring for 3 infants of the ages 3 months old and two 17 months old. The 3 month old infant was found asleep in a restrictive device. This person was identified as a volunteer by the director, but has been present at the operation consistently. There are no training records for this person.
